audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Trundle / Trundle / Trundle / Skill / Trundle / Trundle / Skill — five stages to Trundle — while Trundle loses this lane at 48.20% over 583 games, the largest sample of any matchup in my slice. The whys underneath give a completely different and internally consistent picture: whys[0] "Level 1 is a neutral last-hit lane", whys[1] "Level 2 stays even", whys[3] "At 4-5 he pulls ahead", whys[4] "Level 6 is even", whys[6] "Two items in he reclaims the lane".
audit.why: Five of the seven paragraphs contradict their own labels, and unlike most of this file they contradict them in a coherent way — the prose describes an even start, a Zaahen mid-game, a Trundle level 3 and first item, and a Zaahen late. That reading matches the 48.20% figure; the labels do not.
audit.corrected: Skill at levels 1, 2 and 6; Trundle at level 3 and first item; Zaahen at levels 4-5 and two-plus items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names Zaahen's ultimate at all — breakdown.cooldowns literally reads "Zaahen Ultimate (verify): His power spike — verify the exact name + effect on the live patch", and tldr, winCon, loading, report[5] and dosFull[0] all say "Ultimate". Cultivation of War is absent from both layers.
audit.why: The kit library has the answers. The ultimate is Grim Deliverance, 110/95/80 seconds at 600 range: he rises, stabs downward, and heals for a portion of the damage dealt — a heal on his biggest cooldown, which is why anti-heal timing decides the level-6 exchange rather than raw damage. And his passive is the bigger omission: Cultivation of War stacks Determination off attacks and abilities against champions for bonus Attack Damage, and Riot's text says that when it is filled he gains increased Attack Damage AND CAN REVIVE. A revive is not a detail — it changes what "you won the duel" means.
audit.corrected: Grim Deliverance: 110/95/80s, heals for a portion of damage dealt. Cultivation of War: Determination stacks into bonus AD and a revive when filled.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two of Zaahen's abilities are called by names that do not exist. "E Golden Onslaught" appears in spikes[1], wants.foe[1], early, mid, whys[1] and whys[3] — six times. "R Final Retribution" appears in spikes[2], wants.foe[2], mid and whys[4] — four times.
audit.why: The E is Aureate Rush and the R is Grim Deliverance. Ten fabricated ability names in one matchup, and the packet's near-miss detector raised nothing because the invented names are nowhere near the real ones — the same failure mode as "Ares of Blaze" for Pyroclasm. A player reading this page and then reading his own client will not be able to map one onto the other.
audit.corrected: E = Aureate Rush (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s dash). R = Grim Deliverance (110/95/80s). Q is The Darkin Glaive.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json raises four interactions for this exact matchup and none of them appears on the page: Pillar of Ice denying Aureate Rush, anti-heal against The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance, Aureate Rush bypassing stacked resistances, and The Darkin Glaive being an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: The first is the whole matchup: Pillar of Ice shuts off Aureate Rush, so it should be held for his engage rather than spent on poke — and at 21 seconds against his 10, that discipline is the only way one pillar covers two dashes. Dreaded Return is the other missing piece entirely: an 850-range stab that PULLS enemies toward him, which is how a Trundle standing on Frozen Domain gets taken off it. Neither the pull nor the pillar interaction is mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.corrected: Hold Pillar of Ice for Aureate Rush (10s), not for poke. Dreaded Return (14s, 850 range) pulls you off your own zone.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] calls Subjugate a "true-damage drain", and spikes[2] describes it only as draining him "hard".
audit.why: Subjugate deals magic damage — 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health — steals 40% of armour and MR, heals Trundle for the damage amount, and doubles the stolen figure over 4 seconds. Calling it true damage tells a player his ultimate ignores magic resist, which changes both his own build and his read on when the ultimate is worth pressing.
audit.corrected: Subjugate is magic damage: 40% of resists plus a fifth of max health, healing the same, doubling over 4s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not a single cooldown number appears in either layer; breakdown.cooldowns is a placeholder asking someone to verify the ultimate's name.
audit.why: The Darkin Glaive 10/9/8/7/6s, Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Grim Deliverance 110/95/80s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s. Two numbers do the work: Aureate Rush at 10 seconds against Pillar of Ice at 21 means the pillar only ever answers one of two dashes, and Grim Deliverance at 110 seconds against Subjugate's 120 means he gets his ultimate back first.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], dontsFull[1], loading, mid and two whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] spends the first back on "Core component + boots (≈1300g)" and no field in either layer mentions anti-heal.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal against The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance, and the kit backs it: the Q heals him on a 10-second cooldown at rank 1 and the ultimate heals him for a portion of all the damage it deals. Against two healing sources on top of a passive that can revive him, Grievous Wounds before the first extended trade matters more here than a Trinity Force component.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling (≈800g) on the first back — The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance both heal him.

audit.why: The packet raised zero defects and zero suspectNames for this matchup, which is itself the finding: ten fabricated ability names slipped through because the near-miss detector only catches names close to real ones. Any matchup whose packet is clean is not therefore verified. The full layer's own "(verify)" placeholder in breakdown.cooldowns is the honest marker and I have now filled it from the kit library.

notes: This is the worst-named page in my slice. Zaahen's E is called "Golden Onslaught" six times and his R "Final Retribution" four times; the real names are Aureate Rush and Grim Deliverance. The packet flagged zero defects and zero suspectNames here, which is worth knowing on its own — the near-miss detector only catches names close to real ones, so a clean packet is not evidence a page is correct. The full layer was at least honest about it: breakdown.cooldowns carried a literal "(verify): verify the exact name + effect on the live patch" placeholder, which I have filled from the kit library. Two things the page never mentions that decide the matchup: Dreaded Return is an 850-range stab that PULLS you toward him, which is how a Trundle gets taken off Frozen Domain, and Cultivation of War lets him REVIVE at full Determination. All four of the interactions _missing-interactions.json raises for this matchup were absent and are now placed. Chart was Trundle 5/7 over a 48.20% win rate across 583 games.
